bugs: app/Imports/ImportStockLevels.php:74 puts the raw quantity cell into the error message. A file with non-UTF-8 bytes in that cell (for example a Latin-1 export) makes response()->json throw 'Malformed UTF-8 characters' and the endpoint returns 500. Probe: "sku,quantity\nA,\xff\xfe\nB,2" gave 500. Because it flushes chunks as it goes, valid rows may already be written when the client gets the 500.

Treats the first non-blank line as the header instead of line 1. A file starting with a blank line is accepted (200) rather than handled as a file without a header row. This is lenient and the line numbers stay correct, but it departs from 'the header is line 1'.
antipatterns: app/Imports/ImportStockLevels.php:74 echoes untrusted cell content into the JSON response without making sure it is valid UTF-8
app/Imports/ImportStockLevels.php:41-90 is one long procedural loop: header detection, validation as an if/elseif chain, and chunk flushing all mixed together
app/Imports/ImportStockLevels.php:80-83 writes chunks while streaming with no transaction, so a later failure leaves a partial import that the client is never told about
app/Http/Controllers/StockImportController.php:11 uses a single-action 'store' controller where an invokable controller would be the more natural Laravel choice (minor)
strengths: Streams the file with fgets and flushes upserts every 500 rows, so memory stays bounded; the file handle is closed in a finally
Lets Eloquent upsert fill in the timestamps instead of setting them by hand
Uses mb_strlen for the 255-character sku limit, which matches how string columns count length
Error messages are precise (column count found vs expected, and the bad value is echoed back)
Tests assert specific validation messages (assertJsonValidationErrors with message fragments), use sole() and named datasets, and cover blank-line counting, BOM/CRLF, overflow, chunking and 5 MB

bugs: Keeps every valid row in the $quantities array until the end of the file (app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:47). The 5 MB cap bounds this, so it is not a real bug, but memory is not streamed the way impl-1's is.
antipatterns: app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:51 `$columns ?? $this->columns('');` relies on a side effect (an exception) to reject empty files; an explicit check would read more clearly
app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:136-143 sets created_at/updated_at by hand even though Eloquent::upsert already adds the timestamps and appends updated_at to the update columns
app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:124 has a redundant overflow check: strlen>10 and (int)>MAX together, where a single digits regex like \d{1,10} would do
app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:107 parse() returns array|string, using the string as an error signal; a stringly-typed union where a small result type or early-return structure would be clearer
app/Actions/ImportStockLevels.php:120 strlen counts bytes, not characters, for the 255 limit, so multibyte skus are rejected sooner than the column requires
strengths: Never echoes untrusted cell content into the response, so malformed encodings still return a clean 200 with a per-line error (probe confirmed)
Treats line 1 strictly as the header, which matches the spec; empty, semicolon-delimited and headerless files all return 422
A generator with try/finally keeps the line reading and file-handle cleanup in one place, and the main loop reads cleanly
Validation happens before any write, then a single chunked upsert through a collection pipeline, so the header check can never leave a partial import
Invokable controller plus an Action class plus a FormRequest with mimes:csv,txt|max:5120

Thorough Pest tests: an annotated line-number fixture, a dataset of bad quantities (including 1e3, +5 and a 20-digit overflow), a header-width check, an exact 5 MB boundary, the chunking path and non-file input

v.rationale: I ranked impl-2 first. Both suites pass (impl-2: 29 tests, impl-1: 25), and the two designs are close: a FormRequest with mimes:csv,txt|max:5120, a thin controller, an invokable importer that reads lines with fgets and str_getcsv(escape:''), header lookup that ignores case and surrounding spaces, BOM stripping, and chunked upserts. The ranking comes down to how each handles untrusted input. impl-1 puts the raw quantity cell into its error message. When a warehouse file has non-UTF-8 bytes in that cell, the JSON encoder throws and the endpoint returns 500, which I confirmed with a probe. And because impl-1 flushes upserts while it streams, valid rows may already be saved when the client sees the failure. That is a real failure on exactly the task's focus: messy real-world files whose bad rows should be reported, not crash the request. impl-2 never echoes cell content, so the same file returns 200 with a line-2 error. impl-2 also follows 'the header is line 1' strictly, while impl-1 quietly treats the first non-blank line as the header. impl-1 does have some edges: it streams memory better, lets Eloquent handle the upsert timestamps, measures sku length with mb_strlen, and its tests check validation messages more precisely. impl-2 has small ceremony issues: timestamps set by hand, the `$columns ?? $this->columns('')` side-effect trick, a redundant overflow check, and the array|string return type. These cost it some simplicity points but don't outweigh impl-1's 500 bug. Other probes behaved the same in both: quoted fields containing commas parse correctly, binary data with a .csv name gets 422, and empty or extra-column rows give the right line errors. All probe files were deleted afterwards.
